issues.body:
Both markers this PR adds stamp [SONNET-4.6] — gui/app/src/data/tools.ts:151 and gui/README.md:165 ('[SONNET-4.6] This is the honest live-wasm boundary') — while the commit carrying them (91b16895) is trailered 'Co-Authored-By: GPT-5.6 Sol <[redacted-email]>'. The marker and the trailer disagree inside one commit.

AGENTS.md:152 (item 5) requires the inline [MODEL] marker and the Co-Authored-By trailer to be derived from the harness's actual runtime model, and to agree. AGENTS.md:167 names this precise string as the canonical failure case: attribution must be correct, 'not false markers (e.g. [SONNET-4.6]) left over from an earlier brief generation'.

This is metadata, not behaviour, so it does not block. It matters for the reason the rule exists: multi-model diffs are re-reviewed per model, and because these are durable source comments rather than commit metadata, a mislabelled span routes this work to the wrong re-review lane permanently. The correct marker for this author is well established — [GPT-5.6] appears 60 times under gui/ and packages/, including a neighbouring N3 comment at engine-context.tsx:917 inside the very block this README paragraph documents.
issues.fix_hint: Replace [SONNET-4.6] with [GPT-5.6] at gui/app/src/data/tools.ts:151 and gui/README.md:165, matching the commit trailer and the existing [GPT-5.6] stamps in gui/app/src/lib/engine-context.tsx. Do not touch the pre-existing [OPUS-4.8] / [FABLE-5] stamps elsewhere in these files — per AGENTS.md:449 those are accurate history and must never be rewritten.
issues.title: Unchanged from round 2: [SONNET-4.6] marker contradicts the commit's own Co-Authored-By: GPT-5.6 Sol trailer

issues.body:
gui/app/src/data/tools.ts:151 attributes the N3 work to 'sq-bfimm'. That id still occurs exactly once in the whole repository — this line. The README hunk in this same PR attributes the same feature to sq-glo5r (gui/README.md:141), and sq-glo5r is the id every existing N3 reference uses: engine-context.tsx:426 and :878, workspace-context.tsx, packages/sparq-client/src/workspace.ts, inference-tool.tsx, workbench.tsx, file-ingest.ts, gui/e2e-playwright/specs/n3-inference.web.spec.ts:1, and research/gui-consolidation-fix-plan.md.

So one feature carries two different bead ids in two files of one PR. I could not adjudicate whether sq-bfimm is a typo or a real-but-unreferenced bead: .beads/issues.jsonl contains neither id, and the bd CLI is not on PATH here. The finding is therefore the internal inconsistency, which is provable from the diff alone — not a claim that the bead is fabricated.

Impact is traceability only: a reader grepping sq-bfimm for the design context gets one self-referential hit.
issues.fix_hint: Change sq-bfimm to sq-glo5r at gui/app/src/data/tools.ts:151 so the blurb comment agrees with this PR's own README hunk and the existing sq-glo5r N3 references. If sq-bfimm is a genuinely distinct bead, cite both ('sq-glo5r / sq-bfimm') so the link to the established id survives.

issues.body:
This PR updates the regime list in gui/README.md, inference-control.tsx (header comment and selector docstring), and the tools.ts blurb. Comments describing the same selector were left behind and now contradict the updated docstrings:

- query-workbench.tsx:71 — 'the per-workspace inference (RDFS / OWL 2 RL) selector, in the action row', on the import of the very component this PR re-documented as Off / RDFS / OWL 2 RL / N3.
- query-workbench.tsx:843 — 'the per-workspace inference regime (queries run with the chosen RDFS / OWL 2 RL entailment applied by the engine)', at the <InferenceControl /> render site.
- workspace-context.tsx:104 — describes the persisted field as 'RDFS / OWL 2 RL entailment' (already noted in round 2), and engine-context.tsx:56 describes the lazy-loaded bundle as the 'RDFS / OWL 2 RL reasoner' although the N3 path at :892 loads the same bundle. These two are the same gap, listed for completeness rather than as an additional finding.

Deliberately excluded: reason-wasm.ts:89 is correct as written — it is narrowed to "rdfs" | "owl-rl" on purpose and self-documents that N3 calls reasonN3 directly and never maps through modeToProfile. Filed against gui/README.md because the other paths are outside this diff; the gap is in this PR's sweep, not in those files' original authorship.
issues.fix_hint: Extend the same one-line edit to query-workbench.tsx:71 and :843, and optionally workspace-context.tsx:104 and engine-context.tsx:56, changing 'RDFS / OWL 2 RL' to 'RDFS / OWL 2 RL / N3'. Leave reason-wasm.ts:89 alone — its narrowing is intentional and already explained in place.
issues.title: Unchanged from round 2: doc-sync sweep still misses sibling comments describing the same selector as RDFS / OWL 2 RL only

verdict.summary: Round 3. The diff is unchanged from round 2 in every hunk, so all three prior findings stand, at the same severities, with no new ones — stagnant, not regressing. I re-verified the substance from the checkout rather than inheriting round 2's conclusion, because a doc-only diff that asserts behaviour is exactly where overclaim hides. Every claim holds. The selector really offers N3: WORKSPACE_INFERENCE_MODES is ["off","rdfs","owl-rl","n3"] (packages/sparq-client/src/workspace.ts:81-86) and inference-control.tsx renders one button per entry, so the docstring edit describes the rendered control, not an aspiration. The README's N3 paragraph matches engine-context.tsx:892-925 line for line: enabled docs are filtered (d.enabled !== false), their texts joined, the base folded to N-Triples via storeToNTriples, concatenated, passed to reasoner.reasonN3, and base+derived loaded as the closure. The cache key is n3:<storeEpoch>:<fnv1a(rulesText)>, so toggling or editing a rule invalidates the prior closure even when the store epoch is unchanged — the correctness property that makes 'each document can be enabled, disabled, or removed independently' true at query time rather than only in the UI. The ground-triples-only caveat is not a hedge over a gap: it restates reasonN3's own documented contract at crates/sparq-reason-wasm/src/lib.rs:180-190 ('Only ground facts are returned (rules / formulae / variables are consumed by reasoning)'). No ZK/MPC or other honesty-gated surface is touched, and no performance number is introduced. The three findings are metadata hygiene with zero runtime or user-facing effect: a model marker contradicting the commit's own trailer, a bead id that resolves nowhere, and a doc-sync sweep that stopped short of three sibling comments describing the same selector. None is a blocker or major, so none holds the PR; all three are a single cheap follow-up commit on this branch, and they have now survived two rounds unaddressed.
